sourceReference:
ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g4-arts-music-u05-l02

Lesson focus: community traditions

Resource type: ACADEMY_ORIGINAL_MODEL

MODEL A — “One relationship at a time.” Observation records what is present; interpretation makes a supported claim about meaning or effect; context uses verified information beyond the work. Keeping those layers separate prevents assumptions about a maker, culture, or intention from being presented as evidence. Worked example for community traditions: “Six arrows stop at a border” is observation. “The interruption may suggest restricted movement” is an interpretation supported by that detail. Starting state: state the intended effect, question, or criterion before acting. First decision: locate specific visible, audible, textual, spatial, or process details plus a cited source claim. Intermediate state: complete one bounded study, loop, map, or comparison while most features stay stable. Check: cite what changed before judging it. Finished or intentionally partial result: keep the evidence even when it challenges the first intention. Common misapplication: Guessing identity, culture, or intent from style alone turns an assumption into a claim. Legitimate variation: another learner may choose different which defensible claim to pursue, response format, evidence to prioritize, question to leave open, whether the criteria support revision and still meet the criterion. Source boundary: this invented Academy example teaches analysis procedure only. It is not evidence about a real creator, community, tradition, place, or historical event. Make a real-world context claim only when a substantive cited source is already supplied and accessible; if none is available, label that limitation and keep the response scoped to the Academy example. Use it to study community traditions; describe evidence before judging and adapt the demonstrated relationship rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Manuel Academy resource in this package. It gives you the model, example, or help sheet needed for this task.

Rights: Manuel Academy original; licensed CC BY 4.0 for learner use and adaptation. No third-party text, image, score, lyric, melody, recording, or performance is included.

Access and materials: Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
critique_criteria: The submission contains the required work blocks and one reviewable process state; each required artifact, study, response, or process note can be located.
The learner locates relevant specific visible, audible, textual, spatial, or process details plus a cited source claim and explains how the evidence relates to the stated intent, claim, or criterion.
The learner states an intent or claim and supports it with observable evidence while retaining ownership of artistic decisions.
The process record shows a check and a learner-chosen revision or reasoned decision to keep the result.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Use a written analysis, labelled plan, evidence table, notation, diagram, or private artifact check that preserves the stated target. No microphone, camera, recording, or public audience is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: Anything you have to study will also come as plain text, a described version, or a version you can touch.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
No public performance, voice recording, photo, or camera use is ever required; provide a private, written, or no-audio alternative for every task.
Use only original student work, public-domain material, or properly licensed excerpts; never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or protected works.
The final product must remain the student’s own authorship; adult or AI assistance may support planning and feedback but must not create the graded work.

media.fallback: Use the complete adjacent verbal description and recreate the relationships with raised or movable paper forms. The required Academy model is attached; no outside search is needed.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce community traditions to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one specific visible relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact specific visible evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from specific visible, audible, textual, spatial, or process details plus a cited source claim; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply community traditions under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on community traditions rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
